messages:
katie: Quick sync — thinking about autoscaler behavior when dedicated pools hit cold GPU shortage. Two concerns: operator liveness when many tenants request prewarm and cost-surge. Thoughts?
ajay: do you mean operator OOM / API throttle or tenants getting 503s?
katie: both. Operator sometimes stalls in heavy admission churn in sim. Prewarm credits get exhausted, then we do mass eviction -> oscillation :grimacing:
marco: we've seen that. My proposal: split admission into two surfaces: "fastpath" (burst tokens) and "backfill" (provision intent). Fastpath handled by runtime-agent (low-latency), backfill by planner (batch). Keep operator minimal.
katie: yes. How to size fastpath headroom? static % vs percentile-driven?
leo: percentile-driven by 99p of per-tenant qps over 10m window + add lump-sum for known spikes. Avoid per-minute reactive scaling for prewarm.
ajay: downside: using 99p uses more GPUs. Could we use token-bucket whose refill rate is adaptive? Example config: 
```
fastpath:
  headroom_percentile: 0.99
  burst_tokens_per_tenant: 3
  token_refill_rate_per_min: 1
backfill:
  max_provision_rate_per_min: 2
  lookahead_seconds: 60
```
marco: +1. Also enforce global circuit breaker: max_new_nodes_per_min to avoid noisy neighbor.
katie: operator liveness: when admission storms cause many create/delete events, controller GC loops thrash. Maybe move rate-limited creates to planner and only hand controlplane a small "warm pool" to maintain.
leo: what about model coldstart variance? quantized models warm faster. We could route initial traffic to quantized fallback until full-precision model warms KV cache.
ajay: need safety around quality regression, tie to rollout metadata in model catalog. Auto-fallback only if eval pass or explicit policy.
infra-bot: deploy-check: "autoscaler-circuit-breaker v2" job queued, test cluster id: qc-7
marco: fairness: ensure billing aligns — if tenant consumes fastpath tokens, they pay premium burst fees. Otherwise we get cost shift.
katie: question: where to enforce billing? control plane should log token usage; operator should not be aware of billing. Keep separation.
leo: also need better telemetry: per-tenant warmup latency histogram, per-model kv-cache-hit-rate, prewarm-failures.
ajay: operational playbook: if operator thrash detected, we do conservative fallback: deny fastpath, throttle backfill, and mark degraded.
katie: implementation plan: small RFC PR to add fastpath token API + planner backfill hook. Can people volunteer to review? @marco @leo
marco: I can review. Will sketch CRD changes.
leo: +1, will add observability queries.
katie: thanks. Next step: I'll open RFC with config prototype and a sim run. Reaction :eyes:
infra-bot: note: scheduled sim run at 2026-03-22T00:30Z, job id sim-20260322-01
ajay: can we add test that injects model coldstart delay and quantized fallback path? good to have in sim.
